title: The old tree study
goal: Construct trunk, canopy masses and selective bark texture.
kit: 2H, HB, 2B, 4B, 6B; kneaded eraser; clean stump; medium-tooth paper.

steps.title: Study the reference
steps.text: Look at the trunk direction and large canopy masses before noticing leaves. Identify openings that reveal the sky.
steps.talk: Study the reference. Look at the trunk direction and large canopy masses before noticing leaves. Identify openings that reveal the sky. Pause the narration and practise on paper. Before continuing, ask yourself: Can you describe the tree’s main gesture?
steps.check: Can you describe the tree’s main gesture?

steps.title: Light block-in
steps.text: Place the trunk axis, canopy width and ground contact. Compare total height with canopy width.
steps.talk: Light block-in. Place the trunk axis, canopy width and ground contact. Compare total height with canopy width. Pause the narration and practise on paper. Before continuing, ask yourself: Are the proportions believable?

steps.title: Refine the construction
steps.text: Branch from thicker to thinner structures. Place canopy masses around the branch system.
steps.talk: Refine the construction. Branch from thicker to thinner structures. Place canopy masses around the branch system. Pause the narration and practise on paper. Before continuing, ask yourself: Do branches taper away from the trunk?
steps.check: Do branches taper away from the trunk?

steps.title: Three-value map
steps.text: Group light canopy, middle foliage and dark trunk or interior gaps.
steps.talk: Three-value map. Group light canopy, middle foliage and dark trunk or interior gaps. Pause the narration and practise on paper. Before continuing, ask yourself: Does the tree read in three tones?
steps.check: Does the tree read in three tones?

steps.title: Five values and layers
steps.text: Layer overlapping foliage masses, deepening interiors rather than outlining every leaf.
steps.talk: Five values and layers. Layer overlapping foliage masses, deepening interiors rather than outlining every leaf. Pause the narration and practise on paper. Before continuing, ask yourself: Are the deepest darks within the canopy?
steps.check: Are the deepest darks within the canopy?

steps.title: Selective blending
steps.text: Soften distant canopy edges and some internal passages. Keep a few foreground clusters firm.
steps.talk: Selective blending. Soften distant canopy edges and some internal passages. Keep a few foreground clusters firm. Pause the narration and practise on paper. Before continuing, ask yourself: Is the canopy varied rather than uniformly sharp?
steps.check: Is the canopy varied rather than uniformly sharp?

steps.title: Lift the lights
steps.text: Lift a few small sky holes and lights on branches. Avoid evenly spaced holes.
steps.talk: Lift the lights. Lift a few small sky holes and lights on branches. Avoid evenly spaced holes. Pause the narration and practise on paper. Before continuing, ask yourself: Are the openings irregular?

steps.title: Texture and detail
steps.text: Add broken vertical bark marks that follow trunk curvature, plus a few leaf clusters near the focal area.
steps.talk: Texture and detail. Add broken vertical bark marks that follow trunk curvature, plus a few leaf clusters near the focal area. Pause the narration and practise on paper. Before continuing, ask yourself: Does bark wrap around the trunk?
steps.check: Does bark wrap around the trunk?

steps.title: Final accents and edges
steps.text: Deepen root contact and a small branch junction. Remove repetitive leaf marks.
steps.talk: Final accents and edges. Deepen root contact and a small branch junction. Remove repetitive leaf marks. Pause the narration and practise on paper. Before continuing, ask yourself: Does the tree feel grounded and structurally connected?
steps.check: Does the tree feel grounded and structurally connected?

source: Original AI-generated graphite reference. Intermediate images are analytical contour and value views of this same reference, not hand-drawn stages.
drill: Repeat the study at half size without the grid. Compare your darkest dark, lightest light and largest shape before adding detail.
